newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Miners lead Australian stocks lower at open.
newsitem.headline: Miners lead Australian stocks lower at open.

text.p: The Australian share market softened at the open on Tuesday with miners leading the way lower after base metals prices fell sharply in offshore markets.
The All Ordinaries index shed seven points to 2,359.0.

A second straight session of light gains on Wall Street proved insufficient to overcome the effect of weaker metals prices, the All Resources losing nearly half percent early, compared to broader market losses of just 0.2 percent.
Industrials stocks were mixed in modest trade.
"A disappointing day," said broker Kevin Lourey of Melbourne-based brokerage Peake Lands Kirwan.
"We believed with the fairly positive tone on Wall Street we were going to do better," he said, adding that weaker base metals prices had overshadowed the stronger Dow finish.
"Metals prices were poor and that is really the cause of the malaise in our market at the moment."
In the resource leaders, gold/nickel miner WMC took most punishment, losing about 0.7 percent to A$7.65 (US$7.92) in early trade, but nearly all the major base metals miners incurred some losses.

In the industrials, conglomerate Pacific Dunlop lost ground, dipping 8.9 cents to an intraday low of A$3.10, as U.S. court action revived concerns over its liability for faulty pacemaker leads from its former subsidiary, Telectronics.
Giant retailer Coles Myer Ltd topped turnover with nearly five milion shares traded as the company went ex-dividend 12 cents. Its shares were nine cents lower at A$5.88.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about 10 to nine, while about 50 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
